sentences.text:
(ORAL)
Darshan Singh Vs.
The State

Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the appeal filed against the order of conviction dated 12.03.2020 and order on sentence dated 13.03.2020 passed by Ld. ACMM-I, Patiala House Courts,
New Delhi.

2. The brief facts of the case as per record are that accused was running an establishment in the name of M/s Jagdamba Sweets at RZ-290/17, Jagdamba Road, Tughlakabad Extension, New Darshan Singh vs .

The State on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116539014/
1 Delhi-110019.

On 31.10.2013, Food Safety Officer Sh. Ranjeet Singh alongwith Field Assistant Sh.
Raj Pal Singh and Field Assistant Sh. Siya Ram, as per the instructions of Sh. Shyam Lal, Designated Officer, visited the said establishment, where accused was found conducting the business of various food articles including Khoya Roll which was lying in an open steel tray bearing no label declaration.
The said sample was divided into three parts and packed as per Rules.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
As per the report of Analyst, the sample was found to be unsafe because total dye content of the synthetic colour used exceeded the prescribed maximum limit of 100 ppm.
The report also stated that the sample contained aluminum leaves which is injurious to health.
The said analysis was carried out during the period 01.11.2013 to 13.11.2013 and the result was prepared on 13.11.2013.
3. As the sample failed to pass the test, prosecution was launched by Food Safety Officer by filing complaint with the court.
Accused was summoned to face the trial.
Darshan Singh Vs. The State 2/6

4. Notice of accusation was served upon the accused for violation of Section 26 (2) (i) of Food Safety & Standards Act read with Section 3 (1) (zz) (v) FSSA Act, punishable under Section 59 (i) of FSSA Act, 2006 in these facts and circumstances.

5. After trial, vide judgment dated 12.03.2020, accused was convicted for the violation of provisions of Section 26 (2) (I) of FSSA Act read with Section 3 (I) (zz) (v) of FSSA Act punishable under Section 59 (I) of FSSA Act, 2006 and vide order dated 13.03.2020, convict was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 3 months and fine of Rs.50,000/- and in default of fine, further simple imprisonment for 1 month.
6.
I have heard the arguments and have perused the Trial Court record.

7. In the present case, the counsel for the convict/accused has pointed out that the Referral Food Laboratory, Mysore and Food Analyst had indicated different tests for ascertaining the presence of Silver leaf/Aluminum leaf in the sample lifted in the present case.

While the Food Analyst has indicated the test as "Nitric Acid test", the RFL has indicated the method of test as "Inorganic Chemistry by Vogel".
8.

Therefore, the difference in the description of the test, in the Food Analyst report and in the report of RFL, Mysore, has been used by the Ld. Counsel to contend that the test used by the RFL in the present case is not in consonance with the Food Safety and Regulation Rules, 2011; more specifically, Rule 2.4.2 Darshan Singh Vs. The State 3/6 (7) which reads as follows:
The manuals of the method of analysis, as amended/adopted by the Authority from time to time including AOAC/ISO/Pearsons/Jacob/IUPAC/Food Chemicals CODEX/
BIS/Woodmen/Winton- Winton/Joslyn, shall be used for analysing the samples of food articles.

However, in case the method for analysing any parameter is not available in these manuals, a validated method of analysis prescribed by Darshan Singh vs . The State on 17 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116539014/
2
internationally recognized/analytic/regulatory agencies, shall be adopted.
(Emphasis supplied).

9. Ld. Counsel submits that the description of the test in the RFL, Mysore's report does not indicate that it is a test given in one of the prescribed journal/literature i.e. in AOAC, ISO, Pearsons, Jacob,
IUPAC, Food Chemicals CODEX, BIS, Woodmen, Winton-Winton, Joslyn.
Counsel further submits that any other method can only be adopted if no method is indicated in the aforesaid prescribed journals.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the counsel.
11. I have also put to the Ld. CPP, who is appearing in the present matter, whether he is in a position to answer the question raised by the counsel as a question of law.

12. Ld. CPP fairly submits that whether no test method is indicated in the AOAC, ISO, Pearsons,
Jacob, IUPAC, Food Chemicals CODEX, BIS, Woodmen, Winton-Winton, Joslyn, to test the presence of Silver and Aluminum, is a question of fact.

In the absence of the journals, he is not in a position to answer why Darshan Singh Vs. The State 4/6 Inorganic Chemistry by Vogel has been adopted by the RFL, as also that this is a question to be answered by the Expert, who has applied the test.

entities.text: Darshan Singh Vs. The State 4/6 Inorganic Chemistry by Vogel
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 13. Although, it is settled law that findings given by RFL cannot be questioned, but the report can always be questioned on why a particular method is adopted when, prima facie, it does not seem to be in consonance with rule concerned.

Reliance is placed upon the decision in Nestle India Limited Vs. The Food Safety and Standards, 2015 SCC OnLine Bom 4713 and more specifically, on paragraph no. 92, which is quoted hereinbelow for ease of reference:

entities.text: Nestle India Limited Vs. The Food Safety and Standards, 2015 SCC OnLine Bom 4713
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no manner of doubt that this Court is not expected to see the correctness or otherwise of the reports given by the experts and, therefore, there cannot be any dispute regarding ratio of the judgments on which reliance has been placed by the learned and the learned Additional Solicitor General for Respondent No.1.

This Court, however, can see whether the samples have been properly analysed in terms of the mandatory provisions of the Act or not and, secondly, whether any reliance can be placed either on reports obtained by the Respondents or even for that matter on the reports obtained by the Petitioner.
(Emphasis supplied)
14. In the present case, evidence would have to be led to show that the test method employed by the RFL falls within the exception provided in the Regulation 2.4.2(7).
In my view, the burden to establish this from the very beginning is on the Darshan Singh Vs. The State 5/6 prosecution.
15. In any event, considering the aforesaid question of fact, which has arisen in the present case, I am of the view that additional evidence is required to be recorded.
Therefore, the matter is being remanded back to the Trial Court, setting aside the judgment of conviction and sentence with aforesaid direction.

17.
Appeal is disposed off accordingly.
TCR be sent back.
